age.evidence: Adult (postnatal days 60-70) male and female SpragueDawley rats were used for all experiments

sex.evidence: Adult (postnatal days 60-70) male and female SpragueDawley rats were used for all experiments

dosing.evidence: Psilocybin (NIDA Drug Supply Program) was dissolved in 0.9% saline (vehicle)... Separate groups of rats (n = 12-15 per group) were administered doses of 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 mg/kg intraperitoneally (i.p.), according to the body weight of each animal (1 µl/g).

handling.evidence: not reported; no handling protocol is described in the methods.

group_housing.evidence: All animals were pair housed with a conspecific of the same sex in wire-topped, plastic cages (27 × 48 × 20 cm)

day_night_flipped.evidence: All animals were maintained in the animal housing facility on a 12-hour reverse light-dark cycle (lights off at 8:00 am)

enrichment_housing.evidence: plastic cages (27 × 48 × 20 cm) with filter tops and standard enrichment (toys, tunnels).

assays.assay_name: Spontaneous behavior observation (home-cage-like cage, incl. HTR/WDS)
assays.assay_description: Immediately after i.p. psilocybin (0.5, 1, 1.5 mg/kg) or saline, rats were individually placed in a clean plastic cage (27 × 48 × 20 cm) similar to the home cage and video-recorded for 15 min. Six spontaneous behaviors (HTR/WDS, sniffing/digging, grooming, rearing, circling, immobility) were manually scored in BORIS as bouts and/or duration, analysed in 3-min bins, by correlation matrices and PCA.

application_type.evidence: were administered doses of 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 mg/kg intraperitoneally (i.p.)

setup_habituation.evidence: Immediately following drug or vehicle administration, animals were individually placed in a clean plastic cage; no prior apparatus habituation described.

setup_restrain.evidence: animals were individually placed in a clean plastic cage (27 × 48 × 20 cm)... Behavioral responses in this behavioral setup were recorded for 15 minutes

food_restriction.evidence: Testing in a separate clean plastic cage; no food described in the test cage (ad libitum food only in home housing).

water_restriction.evidence: Testing in a separate clean plastic cage; no water described in the test cage (ad libitum water only in home housing).

time_to_assay.evidence: Immediately following drug or vehicle administration, animals were individually placed in a clean plastic cage

sample_size.evidence: Separate groups of rats (n = 12-15 per group)

outcomes.summary: Acute psilocybin produced dose- and sex-dependent changes in spontaneous behaviors over 15 min. HTR/WDS followed a bell-shaped dose curve peaking at 1 mg/kg; immobility increased with dose; rearing and grooming decreased at all doses; sniffing/digging declined at higher doses (especially in females); circling increased variably by sex (notably females at 1.5 mg/kg). PCA showed a dose-dependent shift from exploratory behaviors toward immobility.
outcomes.statistics: HTR/WDS: main effect of dose p<0.0001; saline vs 1 mg/kg males p<0.05, females p<0.01. Circling: Dose×Sex p<0.05, dose p<0.05; females 1.5 mg/kg vs saline p<0.01. Immobility: Dose×Sex p<0.001, dose p<0.0001, sex p<0.01. Sniffing/digging: Dose×Sex p<0.0001, dose p<0.001, sex p<0.01. Rearing: Dose×Sex p<0.0001, dose p<0.0001, sex p<0.001; reduced at all doses p's<0.05. Grooming: dose p<0.0001; reduced at all doses p's<0.05. Within-session: HTR/WDS Time×Dose p<0.0001; circling Time×Dose×Sex p<0.01; immobility Time×Dose p<0.0001; sniffing/digging Time×Dose×Sex p<0.001; rearing Time×Dose p<0.001; grooming Time×Dose p<0.05.
outcomes.evidence: When compared to saline, psilocybin elicited HTR/WDS following a bell-shaped curve, while immobility increased linearly, with dose. Rearing and grooming decreased markedly even at low doses, sniffing/digging declined only at higher doses, and circling increased variably across doses for each sex.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Table 1: HTR/WDS (bouts), sniffing/digging (bouts and duration), grooming (bouts), rearing (bouts), circling (bouts), immobility (bouts and duration) = 8 measures.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Behavioral responses (see Table 1) were quantified in 3-minute intervals to evaluate how distinct behaviors emerged and evolved throughout the 15-minute observation period.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No transition or sequence analysis; correlations were between total behavior measures.

B4_ethological.evidence: Grooming, rearing, and sniffing/digging scored as distinct acts (Table 1).

B5_social.evidence: animals were individually placed in a clean plastic cage

B6_cognitive.evidence: Spontaneous behaviors were operationally defined as behaviors that occurred naturally and inherently without inducing a change in the external environment or providing any exploratory context.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Behavioral scoring was performed manually by trained observers using Behavioral Observation Research Interactive Software (BORIS)

B8_multivariate.evidence: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was conducted to reduce the dimensionality of the dataset to identify patterns in the distribution of behavioral variables

E1_environment_type.evidence: animals were individually placed in a clean plastic cage (27 × 48 × 20 cm), which was similar to their home cage

E2_shelter.evidence: No shelter described in the clean test cage.

E3_bedding.evidence: Active nose movements in contact with the home cage bedding, accompanied by scratching of the bedding with the forepaws or the creation of holes in the bedding.

E4_nesting.evidence: No nesting material described in the clean test cage.

E5_enrichment.evidence: Enrichment (toys, tunnels) described for home cages only, not the clean test cage.

E7_social_context.evidence: Pair-housed animals were tested simultaneously in separate clean cages that were placed 10 cm apart

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water described in the clean test cage during the 15-min recording.

D1_continuity.evidence: Behavioral responses in this behavioral setup were recorded for 15 minutes, then the animals were returned to their home cage together.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Single acute session immediately after injection; study 'only assessed effects of a single dose in naïve rats'.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline recording described; testing began immediately after injection.

D5_followup.evidence: it assesses the acute effects of psilocybin over a short temporal range immediately following drug administration

judge_notes: All candidates identified a single assay; retained as one spontaneous-behavior observation assay (HTR/WDS included as one of the scored behaviors, not a separate assay).
D2: 15-min session scored 1 per rubric (15–60 min inclusive); overrode gemma4's score of 0.
E1: test cage was a clean cage 'similar to' the home cage, not the animal's own housing cage; followed modal Standard apparatus (0) over qwen's Home cage (1).
E3: bedding present per Table 1 operational definition of sniffing/digging; all candidates agreed.
time_dependent set to n/a per rubric (single post-dose timepoint), although within-session Time×Dose interactions were significant (captured under B2).
n_total left null: 'n = 12-15 per group' does not unambiguously define total N across dose×sex groups; qwen's 96 was not explicitly reported.
Age kept as modal 'young_adult' (PND 60-70), noting paper labels them 'Adult'.
